    Why start at 5%?

    Schwab’s 2026 outlook estimated 5.9% annualized for U.S. large-cap stocks and 4.8% for U.S. aggregate bonds over the next decade. A simple 40% stock and 60% bond blend is roughly 5.2% nominal. The 5% default is an illustration you can adjust to reflect your holdings, fees and expectations.

    Federal brackets & deductions

    Ordinary rates apply to successive slices of taxable ordinary income. The selected filing status also determines the standard deduction and qualified-dividend thresholds.

    How the model treats retirement income

    Required minimum distributions

    The estimate uses the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table for an owner who has reached their applicable RMD age, using each account’s December 31, balance. Traditional, SEP and SIMPLE IRA minimums can be combined for the same owner. Enter each employer plan separately outside this planner if you have multiple plans, since one plan’s withdrawal generally cannot satisfy another’s minimum. Roth IRAs and designated Roth 401(k) balances have no lifetime minimum for the original owner. A current-employer plan may allow a delay while you are working, subject to the ownership rule.

    The first RMD can generally be delayed to April 1 of the following year. Add any prior-year minimum due in in the advanced fields. IRA cash withdrawals from the covered IRAs count toward their RMD once, and an RMD is ineligible for conversion. A shortfall can incur a excise tax, reduced to if corrected on time, and a waiver can be available. The projection shows the shortfall separately. Confirm inherited-account minimums, the joint-life table when a sole-beneficiary spouse is more than 10 years younger, and multiple workplace plans separately. An eligible direct qualified charitable distribution from an IRA at age or older can count toward the RMD and be excluded from income. The limit is per eligible owner. The calculator does not model those transfers.

    IRS RMD FAQs · IRS Publication 590-B and lifetime tables

    Traditional withdrawals and IRA-to-Roth conversions

    Pretax cash distributions and the taxable portion of a direct Roth conversion are ordinary income. A conversion moves money between accounts and raises income for tax purposes only. For an IRA with nondeductible basis, enter each owner’s available Form 8606 basis and the combined projected December 31, value of their traditional, SEP and SIMPLE IRAs before the withdrawals and conversion you are modeling. The planner treats the cash flows as year-end events and applies the same pro rata denominator as you move the sliders. For amounts you already know, enter the combined year-end balance plus the applicable distributions and conversions. Confirm Form 8606 treatment for QCDs, outstanding rollovers, recharacterizations or distributions with special exclusions.

    Employer-plan distributions use the taxable percentage you enter. Direct pre-tax plan-to-Roth rollovers have separate plan and reporting rules, so this model’s conversion field is for eligible IRA money only. A conversion can increase taxable Social Security, move qualified dividends into a higher tax band or reduce the senior deduction. Most completed Roth conversions cannot be undone by recharacterizing them.

    IRS Form 8606 instructions · IRS rollover rules

    Roth cash and early withdrawals

    Qualified Roth withdrawals are tax-free. For a nonqualified withdrawal, enter the taxable earnings and, if applicable, the separate amount subject to the additional early-distribution tax. Roth IRAs order regular contributions first, then conversions in order, then earnings. Converted amounts can have a separate five-year recapture period. Nonqualified designated Roth plan withdrawals generally prorate contributions and earnings. Exact tax treatment depends on the account’s history and the owner’s eligibility at the time of withdrawal.

    Many otherwise taxable withdrawals before the applicable age can face an additional tax unless an exception applies. The age-55 separation exception can apply to a qualifying workplace plan and is unavailable for IRAs. Verify any additional tax under Form 5329, including special SIMPLE IRA rates, before using the penalty field.

    IRS Publication 590-B · IRS early distribution exceptions

    Pensions, Social Security and senior deductions

    A pension is generally taxable except for any recovery of after-tax cost. Enter the taxable share from the plan or Form 1099-R if known. The Social Security calculation uses provisional income, which includes one-half of benefits, other modeled taxable income, and tax-exempt interest. Up to of benefits may be included in taxable income. If filing separately, indicate whether you lived with your spouse at any time during the year.

    IRS pension tax rules · IRS Social Security worksheet · IRS Schedule 1-A

    Dividends, interest and savings

    Use box 1b of Form 1099-DIV for qualified dividends and box 1a minus 1b for nonqualified dividends. Qualified dividends and eligible net long-term gains stack above ordinary taxable income at the applicable preferential rates. Taxable interest and nonqualified dividends use ordinary rates. Savings principal is cash without new income. Dividends and gains can be taxable even if reinvested. The reinvestment field reduces available cash only. If you sell taxable investments, enter net gains and enter any separately released principal in the taxable brokerage principal field.

    The model estimates the net investment income tax (NIIT) on the lesser of modeled investment income or AGI above the applicable threshold. Qualified-plan distributions and conversions can raise the income used for the threshold. This simplified calculation assumes no investment expense deductions or foreign-income MAGI adjustments.

    IRS Investment Income and Expenses · IRS net investment income tax

    Limits of the estimate

    The calculator covers U.S. federal regular income tax, modeled NIIT, and user-entered exposure to the early-distribution tax. It uses continuous bracket math. IRS tax-table rounding, alternative minimum tax, credits, payroll tax, withholding, estimated payments, capital-loss carryovers, special capital gains rates, RMD excise tax, and state taxes are outside the calculation. The itemized field accepts a total after applicable limits. It does not calculate those limits or auto-apply special deductions.

    Higher income can affect Medicare income-related premiums two years later under the usual two-year lookback. The dashboard leaves premiums and health-insurance subsidy changes out of the cash projection. Compare plan documents and the applicable tax forms when an amount depends on basis, withdrawal timing or an exception.
